definitions.explanation: eating food while standing, typically at a counter or stall; also refers to establishments where customers eat standing up

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{立|た}ち{食|ぐ}いそばを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I ate at the station's stand-up soba shop.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{食|ぐ}いは{時間|じかん}がないときに{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: Stand-up eating is convenient when you're short on time.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ごはんは{立|た}ち{食|ぐ}いで{済|す}ませた。
examples.english: I finished breakfast at a stand-up eatery.

notes:
FORMATION:
{立|た}つ (to stand) + {食|く}う (to eat - rough) → eating while standing

JAPANESE FOOD CULTURE:
{立|た}ち{食|ぐ}い restaurants are popular in Japan, especially at train stations. They offer quick, affordable meals for busy commuters.

COMMON TYPES:
- {立|た}ち{食|ぐ}いそば (stand-up soba shop)
- {立|た}ち{食|ぐ}いうどん (stand-up udon shop)
- {立|た}ち{食|ぐ}い{寿司|ずし} (stand-up sushi)
- {立|た}ち{飲|の}み (stand-up bar)

NUANCE:
Eating while standing or walking in public (outside of designated areas) is generally considered impolite in Japan, but {立|た}ち{食|ぐ}い at dedicated establishments is completely acceptable.

ALTERNATE READING:
Also read as たちぐい (more common) or たちくい.

RELATED:
- {立|た}ち{飲|の}み (stand-up bar/drinking)
- {食|た}べ{歩|ある}き (eating while walking/food tour)
- {駅|えき}そば (station soba)
